Getting started with ggsaveR

Source: vignettes/ggsaveR.Rmd
ggsaveR.Rmd

ggsaveR replaces ggplot2::ggsave() with a version whose extra behaviour is switched on with global options. The options are set once, at the top of a script, and apply to every ggsave() call that follows. Existing code does not need to change.

library(ggplot2)
library(ggsaveR)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'ggsaveR'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:ggplot2':
#> 
#>     ggsave

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Fuel economy (mpg)", y = "Weight (1000 lb)", colour = "Cylinders")

Without any options, ggsave() behaves as in ggplot2. It returns the paths of the files it wrote, invisibly:

ggsave("plain.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5)

Setting options

ggsaveR_options() sets one or more options, checks them, and returns the previous values so they can be restored:

old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = c("png", "pdf"))
getOption("ggsaveR.formats")
#> [1] "png" "pdf"
options(old)

The same options can be set with options() by prefixing them with ggsaveR., for example options(ggsaveR.formats = c("png", "pdf")). Calling ggsaveR_options() without arguments lists the current values.

Several formats and sizes

The formats option turns one ggsave() call into several files. The extension of filename is replaced by that of each format.

old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = c("png", "pdf"))
print(ggsave("economy.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5))
#> [1] "economy.png" "economy.pdf"
options(old)

Each format can also have its own size, resolution and other ggsave() arguments. Settings in a format take precedence over arguments given in the call, and arguments in the call fill in whatever a format leaves out.

old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = list(
  list(device = "png", width = 180, height = 120, units = "mm", dpi = 300),
  list(device = "pdf", width = 180, height = 120, units = "mm")
))
print(ggsave("economy.png", p))
#> [1] "economy.png" "economy.pdf"
options(old)

File names that describe the size

If two formats would write to the same file, such as a PNG for a journal and a PNG for slides, ggsaveR adds the size to their names:

old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = list(
  list(device = "png", width = 85, height = 60, units = "mm", dpi = 600),
  list(device = "png", width = 254, height = 143, units = "mm", dpi = 150)
))
print(ggsave("economy.png", p))
#> [1] "economy_85x60mm_600dpi.png"   "economy_254x143mm_150dpi.png"
options(old)

The size is the one ggplot2 actually uses, after scale and default dimensions are applied. Raster formats also include the resolution. With size_suffix = TRUE every file gets a size suffix; with FALSE, clashing names are an error. A format can also carry its own suffix:

old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = list(
  list(device = "png", width = 85, height = 60, units = "mm", suffix = "_journal"),
  list(device = "png", width = 254, height = 143, units = "mm", suffix = "_slides")
))
print(ggsave("economy.png", p, dpi = 150))
#> [1] "economy_journal.png" "economy_slides.png"
options(old)

Output folder

dir places every file saved with a relative name in one folder, which is created if needed. Absolute paths are left alone.

old <- ggsaveR_options(dir = "figures")
print(ggsave("economy.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5))
#> [1] "figures/economy.png"
options(old)

Protecting existing files

By default an existing file is overwritten, as in ggplot2. With overwrite_action = "unique", ggsaveR adds a number instead:

old <- ggsaveR_options(overwrite_action = "unique")
ggsave("draft.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5)
ggsave("draft.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5)
#> File exists. Saving to draft-1.png instead.
options(old)

With "stop", an existing file is an error. When several files are saved at once, the check covers all of them before anything is written, and "unique" gives them all the same number so they stay together.

Bypassing ggsaveR for one call

guard = TRUE hands the call unchanged to ggplot2::ggsave(), whatever options are set:

old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = c("png", "pdf"))
ggsave("only-png.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5, guard = TRUE)
options(old)

Scripts that use guard need ggsaveR to be loaded; ggplot2::ggsave() does not know the argument.

Masking

ggsaveR attaches ggplot2 when it is loaded, so its ggsave() takes precedence whichever package is loaded first. ggplot2::ggsave() always reaches the original.
